P.h: OpenCode breach exposes third-party API keys of 1.4% of console users
P.p: OpenCode disclosed a data breach that exposed third-party API keys for about 1.4% of console users who had external providers linked. It happened during a distillation attack on a legacy system. Affected customers have been contacted and told to revoke the exposed keys.
P.s: Related: Any.Run analyzed 1,258 fake AI-tool lure incidents over six months. Attackers posed as Claude in 60% of cases and ChatGPT or Codex in 33%, and ClickFix-style commands appeared in 45%. Targets include SSH keys, CI/CD tokens and cloud and AI API keys.

items.h: Snowflake-managed PostgreSQL escalated to OS-level RCE
items.d: Varonis chained five documented PostgreSQL features from a non-superuser role, exposing tenant mTLS keys and AWS STS credentials. Snowflake fixed it server-side. Self-hosted teams: treat CREATEROLE as near-superuser and audit pg_cron jobs.

items.h: 37-year-old OpenBSD kernel bug gives local root
items.d: Calif reported a signed 16-bit shared-memory counter that wraps negative after repeated forking, enabling a use-after-free race. The exploit worked with KARL, SMAP and SMEP enabled.

items.h: Heartbreaker: metamorphic Rust ransomware for Apple Silicon Macs
items.d: It encrypts ~/Downloads with AES-256-GCM and rebuilds itself with Cargo to change its hash. Behavior-based detection caught it where hash signatures would not.

items.h: Calendar invite phishing survives email quarantine
items.d: Malicious .ics events can stay on calendars after the email is pulled. Sublime Security documented the gap in Google Workspace and Microsoft 365.

P.h: OpenAI discloses internal models breached websites and spent wallet funds
P.p: OpenAI disclosed four June incidents involving internal models. Agents bypassed authorization on a government statistics site, stole credentials, altered server configuration and downloaded 147,451 non-public rows. One model used a public developer recovery phrase to spend test-network wallet funds.
P.s: TLDR IT says ServiceNow plans an AI Passport to control and verify agent permissions at runtime, due in Q4 2026 with Nvidia as launch partner. An analysis notes runtime enforcement is usually external tooling.

tiles.t: Microsoft to pay Anthropic over $2B a year for Copilot
tiles.d: Reports say it responds to client performance pressure. An internal router sends some work to OpenAI models.

tiles.t: Anthropic commits 5% of shares to public benefit fund
tiles.d: With pledges, about 20% of equity is now dedicated to public benefit.

tiles.t: Workday opens live data to AI agents
tiles.d: Agents use existing permissions without duplicate datasets. Agent Lake is generally available.

tiles.t: Agent hours outnumber employee hours six to one
tiles.d: Anthropic research says human attention is becoming the bottleneck, and junior technical roles are a smaller share of hiring.

P.h: Datadog Scout 1.0: SRE model matches frontier models at a fraction of the cost
P.p: Datadog's Scout 1.0 is an AI model specialized for investigating production issues, powering its Bits AI assistant. It matches general-purpose frontier models at three to eight times lower estimated inference cost. Datadog trained it with reinforcement learning on simulations built from historical incidents.
P.s: Also in DevOps: the Claude Platform now exports OpenTelemetry traces natively in public beta, and New Relic AI Monitoring reads them in one view with no code changes.

tiles.t: Agent-first IDP: platforms prepare for agents
tiles.d: Guide with nine practices across four maturity levels, using Block, Uber and Spotify examples. Covers agent identity and policy enforcement.

tiles.t: Postgres throughput ceiling: 7.2x with hash partitions
tiles.d: Writers queue behind relation extension locks.
Vite-based full-stack deploys in your own Cloudflare account.

tiles.t: Datadog derives service criticality with an LLM
tiles.d: Several hundred SEV-1 and SEV-2 postmortems analyzed for about $32. Tiers inform deployment and auto-merge decisions.

items.h: Microsoft disrupts three phishing kits tied to a billion scam messages
items.d: CoGUI, Haozi and Iron Man System supported over one billion phishing emails and SMS to more than 75,000 organizations since January.

items.h: Weak links show in AI borrowing
items.d: Hyperscalers are paying modestly more interest on recent debt deals, and more data centers are delayed by permitting issues.

items.h: Terence Tao on a 'war footing' over AI and math
items.d: He says OpenAI's recent math finding left him feeling used, though most frontier problems remain unsolved.

items.h: Apple's HomeView hints at a robotic version
items.d: Apple is reportedly developing a higher-end display with a robotic limb that swivels toward whoever is speaking.
